note_sections.t: The patient is here for a multidisciplinary re-evaluation regarding treatment options for his known ISUP grade group 3 prostate cancer, following a recent PSA rise to 15.0 ng/mL.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 73-year-old retired bus driver who lives with his partner. He has a history of osteoarthritis, for which he takes paracetamol as needed. His PSA has risen steadily over the past three years, from 4.2 ng/mL in October 2022 to 15.0 ng/mL in March 2025. He reports no urinary complaints, with an IPSS score of 0. He is an alcohol-free individual who enjoys hiking on weekends. He recently attended a cardiology review in autumn 2024, which was stable, and a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins. He also has a known COPD follow-up with pulmonary function testing.

Per rectum, the prostate feels symmetrically enlarged without palpable nodules or induration, consistent with a clinical stage cT1c. The patient is in no acute distress, with a blood pressure of 121/72 mmHg and a heart rate of 64 bpm. His general examination is unremarkable.
